name: application-segmented-page-control
title: Segmented Page Control
description: Dot-style page indicator for paged mobile carousels, with the active dot elongated into a pill and each dot acting as a jump-to-slide button.
useWhen: A carousel or onboarding flow has a small, fixed number of pages (roughly 2-8) that benefit from an at-a-glance position indicator.
You want a compact, low-chrome indicator instead of numbered pagination controls.
Users should be able to tap a dot to jump directly to that slide, not just view progress passively.
avoidWhen: There are many pages (10+) — individual dots stop being scannable; use numbered pagination or a progress bar instead.
The carousel already has visible next/prev arrows and slide count context — dots may be redundant chrome.
You need labeled destinations, not just position — use tabs instead.
responsiveBehavior: The control is an inline-sized flex row that centers naturally under or over a carousel at any width.
accessibility: Uses role="tablist" and role="tab" with aria-selected so the current slide is exposed to assistive tech the same way a tab panel would be.
Each dot has a real, position-specific aria-label ('Go to slide 2, current slide') rather than being purely decorative.
Dots are native <button> elements, keyboard-focusable and activatable without added ARIA.

variants.title: Segmented page control
variants.description: Five-dot indicator with the active second dot shown as an elongated pill.
accessibility: Active state is shown with both shape (pill vs dot) and color, not color alone.

variants.title: Segmented page control (Dark)
variants.description: Segmented page control adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dot colors must meet WCAG AA contrast against dark surfaces.
